subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope and acceptance criteria should this native-Linux VPS performance analysis use before any fix PR is queued?
rationale: The issue is valid but spans many runtime surfaces, and the best next step depends on maintainer intent for whether OpenClaw should own a docs runbook, new instrumentation, code optimizations, or only component-level follow-ups.

options.title: Runbook-first investigation
options.body: Publish a bounded doc/runbook with existing traces, logs, status commands, and explicit missing spans before splitting measured code fixes.

options.title: Rely on narrow PRs
options.body: Treat the bootstrap, MCP, and prep-yield PRs as separate optimizations and leave broader latency attribution uncommitted.

options.title: Decline repository work
options.body: Close as environment-specific support if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own constrained-VPS latency analysis.

recommendation.title: Runbook-first investigation
recommendation.body: Publish a bounded doc/runbook with existing traces, logs, status commands, and explicit missing spans before splitting measured code fixes.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad history across context, memory, subagents, and performance-sensitive agent surfaces makes this the best available owner for the scoping decision.
